title: Hobbycast Episode 15: How to Make Better Game Recommendations
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8UOwBfCgZn8

Daniel (@dungeondive) fields recommendation requests constantly, on the channel and across Facebook groups, BoardGameGeek and Reddit — and thinks most of the answers given are bad, "comically so." The usual failure is simple: people name their favourite game, or whatever they currently happen to be championing, with almost no regard for what was actually asked.

Five fixes. First, **ask questions** — someone who wants "more games like *Rogue Dungeon*" might mean the table footprint, the zero-to-hero arc, the card play, or just that it's a small indie thing, and those point to different shelves. Second, **listen to the answers**, particularly since newcomers often lack the vocabulary to describe what they want. Third, **you don't have to like the game you recommend** — he happily suggests *Gloomhaven*, *Middara* or *HeroQuest* to the right person, and would be doing them no favours by pushing *Secrets of the Lost Tomb*, which is ninety per cent luck. Fourth, **say whether you're vouching for it**, and disclose how much you've actually played. Fifth, **take your time**; forty answers inside two minutes is a sign nobody thought.

His stake in it is community-scale: better recommendations keep newcomers in the hobby, and those newcomers eventually recommend well themselves.

----

What's the best game recommendation you've ever received — and what did the person get right?
